question: Which of the following molecules has triple bond between the two atoms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**N₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The molecule N₂ (Nitrogen) has a triple bond between the two nitrogen atoms.
 
• A triple bond consists of one sigma bond and two pi bonds.
 
• The bond length of a triple bond is shorter compared to single and double bonds, making N₂ a very stable molecule.
 
• Triple bonds are generally stronger and require more energy to break compared to single and double bonds.
 
• N₂ makes up about 78% of the Earth's atmosphere and is essential for all living organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **F₂ (Fluorine)**

 
 
• Contains a single bond between two fluorine atoms.
 
• It is a diatomic molecule and highly reactive.
 
 
 
• **Cl₂ (Chlorine)**
 
 
• Contains a single bond between two chlorine atoms.
 
• It is used in water purification and as a disinfectant.
 
 
 
• **O₂ (Oxygen)**
 
 
• Contains a double bond between two oxygen atoms.
 
• It is essential for respiration in most living organisms.
